text: The observation that antipain inhibits TPA-induced SCEs but not MNNG or MNU induced SCEs can be reconciled by assuming that the molecular events leading to SCEs are rate limited by two factors, recombinational activity and either, by increasing the level of the recombinational enzyme activity or by providing more ONA sites susceptible to these enzymes by introducing DNA gaps and breaks, TPA itself does not damage DNA, therefore any SCE inducing effect is likely to be due to the activation of recombination enzymes, Conversely, ONA-damaging agents probably increase SCEs by activating the substrate rendering it susceptible to constitutive DNA recombinational repair enzymes. The formation of non-sister chromatid exchanges would therefore appear to require at least one rate-limiting process not involved in MNNG or MNU induced SCE formation. Since the process is antipain inhibited, we postulate that it is inducibble2.

Finally, to summarise the possible role of chromosomal changes in multi-step theories o cancer. TA is not the ony promoter and i is highly unlikely that mitotic recombination is the only mechanism of promotion. It seems more incal ments leads to aberrant mitotic segregation events which render certain cells homozygous for the original recessive chromosomal change permitting expression f the malignant phenotype. Bloom's syndrome (in addition to elevated S0E levels), Fanconi's anaemia and ataxia telangiectasia, three human cancer prone diseases, are all characterised by high spontaneous levels of chromosomal instability. It is interesting to speculate in view of the observations made with antipain that chromosome aberrations represent a rate-limiting step in carcinogenesis, probably promotional, mutagenesis alone rarely, if ever achieving complete carcinogenesis. Epidemiological studies of human carcinomas indi cate that several distinct heritable changes are required to convert a normal cell into a malignant cell'. One of the most extensively studied systems in terms of the multi-step nature two-step carcinogenesis has been demonstrated in vivo in the forestomach of the mouse³, in rat colon and bladder and in vitro in cell culture6,7,8 All these systems demonstrate quite convincingly that two qualitatively different processes "initiation" and "promotion", effected by two distinct classes of chemical agent are required for complete carcinogenesis or tumour formation, Initiators are radiation or chemical carcinogens, which when applied at a subcarcinogenic dose cause irreversible mutagenic or epigenetic changes which result in a pre-malignant state, In contrast, promoters are enhance tumour frequency and shorten the lag-time for tumour appearance when applied following an initiator, Thus, it is important to emphasise that a tumour promoter always completes the process begun by an initiator and not vice versa.

have previously proposed s  working hypothesis that initiated cells contain specific recessive autosomal somatic mutations and that promotion results in the expression of these mutations by some aberrant chromosomal segregation event which permits expression of the malignant phenotype (Fig.1). Namely, promotion is some aberrant chromosomal segregation event which converts the heterozygous initiated cell into a hemizygous or homozygous cell, increasing the relative representation of the affected or mutated chromosome segment. This is entirely consistent with the observation that the malignant or transformed phenotype is suppressed on hybridisation with non-transformed cells and that malignant segregants reappear as a result of chromosome loss14,15
